title: Cells Draining to Both Oceans
statement: You are given an m x n grid heights of non-negative integers, where heights[r][c] is the elevation of the cell at row r, column c. Water on a cell flows to any 4-directionally adjacent cell (up, down, left, right) whose height is equal to or lower than the current cell's height. Ocean A borders the top edge (row 0) and the left edge (column 0); Ocean B borders the bottom edge (row m-1) and the right edge (column n-1). A cell drains to an ocean if water starting on it can reach any cell touching that ocean by repeatedly flowing to allowed neighbors (a cell on an ocean's border trivially drains to that ocean). Return the list of [row, col] coordinates of every cell that can drain to BOTH oceans. Order the result in row-major order: sort by row ascending, and within the same row by column ascending. If the grid is empty (no rows, or rows with no columns) or no cell qualifies, return an empty list.
hints: Testing each cell independently by flowing downhill to see if it reaches both edges repeats enormous work. What if you started from the ocean borders instead and walked the flow backwards?

Run a traversal inward from each ocean's border cells. Since real flow goes to equal-or-lower neighbors, the reverse traversal may step only to neighbors with height GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO the current cell. The answer is the intersection of the two reachable sets.

Build two boolean grids. Seed grid A from row 0 and column 0, seed grid B from row m-1 and column n-1. From each seed, DFS/BFS to neighbors where heights[neighbor] >= heights[current], marking them reachable. Finally scan cells in row-major order and collect [r, c] wherever both grids are true.
